subtopics.title: Completing the square and the discriminant

outcomes.text: Complete the square for a quadratic and use the completed form, for example to find a vertex.
Find the discriminant of a quadratic and use it to count real roots, including repeated roots.
Solve quadratic equations and inequalities in one unknown by factorising, completing the square or the formula.
Solve by substitution a pair of simultaneous equations, one linear and one quadratic.
Recognise and solve equations that are quadratic in some function of x.
Understand function, domain, range, one-one function, inverse function and composition of functions.
Find the range of a simple function and the composition of two functions.
Decide whether a function is one-one, and find the inverse in simple cases.
Sketch a one-one function and its inverse, showing the mirror line y = x.
Understand and use transformations y = f(x) + a, f(x + a), af(x), f(ax) and simple combinations.
Find the equation of a straight line from sufficient information.
Use the forms y = mx + c, y - y1 = m(x - x1) and ax + by + c = 0, including distance, midpoint, parallel and perpendicular gradients.
Understand that (x - a)^2 + (y - b)^2 = r^2 is a circle with centre (a, b) and radius r.
Use algebraic methods on problems about lines and circles.
Link a graph to its equation, and use intersections of graphs to solve equations.
Understand radians and convert between radians and degrees.
Use s = r theta and A = half r^2 theta for arc length and sector area in problems.
Sketch and use sine, cosine and tangent graphs for any angle, in degrees or radians.
Use exact trigonometric values for 30, 45 and 60 degrees and related angles.
Use the notations sin^-1, cos^-1 and tan^-1 for principal values of inverse trigonometric functions.
Use the identities tan = sin/cos and sin^2 + cos^2 = 1.
Find all solutions of simple trigonometric equations in a given interval.
Use the expansion of (a + b)^n for positive integer n, including nCr and factorial notation.
Recognise arithmetic and geometric progressions.
Use the nth term and sum formulae to solve problems on progressions.
Use the convergence condition and sum to infinity for a geometric progression.
Understand the gradient of a curve as a limit of chord gradients, and use the notations for first and second derivatives.
Differentiate x^n for rational n, multiples, sums, differences and composites using the chain rule.
Apply differentiation to gradients, tangents, normals, increasing and decreasing functions and rates of change.
Locate stationary points, find their nature, and use them in sketching graphs.
Integrate (ax + b)^n for rational n except -1, with multiples, sums and differences.
Find a constant of integration from given conditions.
Evaluate definite integrals, including simple improper integrals.
Use definite integration to find areas of regions bounded by curves and lines.
Use definite integration to find volumes of revolution about an axis.
Understand modulus, sketch y = |ax + b| and use modulus relations to solve equations and inequalities.
Divide a polynomial of degree up to 4 by a linear or quadratic polynomial, finding quotient and remainder.
Use the factor theorem and the remainder theorem.
Understand how logarithms relate to indices and use the laws of logarithms.
Understand the definition, properties and graphs of e^x and ln x as inverse functions.
Use logarithms to solve equations and inequalities where the unknown is in an index.
Use logarithms to turn a relationship into linear form and find constants from gradient or intercept.
Understand sec, cosec and cot, and use properties and graphs of all six trigonometric functions for any angle.
Use trigonometric identities to simplify, evaluate exactly and solve equations, including compound angle, double angle and R sin(theta + alpha) forms.
Use the derivatives of e^x, ln x, sin x, cos x and tan x with multiples, sums, differences and composites.
Differentiate products and quotients.
Find and use the first derivative of a function defined parametrically or implicitly.
Integrate e^(ax+b), 1/(ax+b), sin(ax+b), cos(ax+b) and sec^2(ax+b) by reversing differentiation.
Use trigonometric relationships, such as double-angle formulae, when integrating.
Understand and use the trapezium rule to estimate a definite integral, including whether it over- or under-estimates.
Locate a root approximately using graphs or a sign change.
Understand a sequence of approximations that converges to a root, and its notation.
Use a given iterative formula x(n+1) = F(x(n)) to find a root to a given accuracy.
Identify the forces acting in a situation, for example with a force diagram.
Understand force as a vector and find and use components and resultants.
Use equilibrium: the vector sum of forces, or components in any direction, is zero.
Understand a contact force as a normal component and a frictional component.
Use the smooth contact model and understand its limitations.
Understand limiting friction and limiting equilibrium, and use F = mu R or F <= mu R.
Use Newton's third law.

topics.title: 4.2 Kinematics of motion in a straight line

outcomes.text: Understand distance and speed as scalars, and displacement, velocity and acceleration as vectors.
Sketch and interpret displacement-time and velocity-time graphs, including gradients and areas.
Use differentiation and integration with respect to time for displacement, velocity and acceleration.
Use constant acceleration formulae for straight-line motion.
Use the definition of linear momentum and understand it is a vector.
Use conservation of linear momentum for direct impact of two bodies, including coalescence.
Apply Newton's laws to a particle of constant mass under constant forces, including friction, tension and thrust.
Use the relationship between mass and weight.
Solve problems on vertical motion and motion on an inclined plane.
Solve problems on connected particles.
Understand work done and calculate it for a constant force with a displacement not parallel to the force.
Understand gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy and use the formulae.
Use the link between energy change and work done, and conservation of energy.
Use power as rate of doing work, and P = Fv for force along the motion.
Solve problems such as a car's instantaneous acceleration on a hill against resistance.
Select a suitable way to present raw data and discuss the pros and cons of representations.
Draw and interpret stem-and-leaf diagrams, box-and-whisker plots, histograms and cumulative frequency graphs.
Use a cumulative frequency graph to estimate medians, quartiles, percentiles and proportions.
Understand and use measures of central tendency and variation, including standard deviation.
Calculate and use the mean and standard deviation, including grouped and coded data, for up to two data sets.
Understand permutation and combination and solve simple selection problems.
Solve problems on arranging objects in a line, including repetition and restrictions.
Evaluate probabilities in simple cases by enumeration or by permutations and combinations.
Use addition and multiplication of probabilities in simple cases.
Understand exclusive and independent events, testing independence by comparing P(A and B) with P(A)P(B).
Calculate and use conditional probabilities in simple cases.
Draw up a probability distribution table for a discrete random variable and calculate E(X) and Var(X).
Use the binomial and geometric probability formulae and recognise when they are suitable models.
Use the expectation and variance formulae for the binomial distribution and the expectation for the geometric distribution.
Understand the normal distribution as a model for a continuous variable and use normal tables.
Solve problems for X ~ N(mu, sigma^2), including finding probabilities and finding unknown parameters.
Recall the conditions for approximating a binomial by a normal, and use it with a continuity correction.
Understand modulus, sketch y = |ax + b| and use modulus relations to solve equations and inequalities.
Divide a polynomial of degree up to 4 by a linear or quadratic polynomial, finding quotient and remainder.
Use the factor theorem and the remainder theorem.
Decompose rational functions into partial fractions for the specified denominator types.
Expand (1 + x)^n for rational n with |x| < 1, including adapted forms and the range of validity.
Understand how logarithms relate to indices and use the laws of logarithms.
Understand the definition, properties and graphs of e^x and ln x as inverse functions.
Use logarithms to solve equations and inequalities where the unknown is in an index.
Use logarithms to turn a relationship into linear form and find constants from gradient or intercept.
Understand sec, cosec and cot, and use properties and graphs of all six trigonometric functions for any angle.
Use trigonometric identities to simplify, evaluate exactly and solve equations, including compound angle, double angle and R sin(theta + alpha) forms.
Use the derivatives of e^x, ln x, sin x, cos x, tan x and tan^-1 x with multiples, sums, differences and composites.
Differentiate products and quotients.
Find and use the first derivative of a function defined parametrically or implicitly.
Integrate e^(ax+b), 1/(ax+b), sin, cos, sec^2 and 1/(x^2 + a^2) forms by reversing differentiation.
Use trigonometric relationships, such as double-angle formulae, when integrating.
Integrate rational functions using partial fractions.
Recognise integrands of the form kf'(x)/f(x) and integrate them.
Use integration by parts when an integrand is a product.
Use a given substitution to simplify and evaluate definite or indefinite integrals.
Locate a root approximately using graphs or a sign change.
Understand a sequence of approximations that converges to a root, and its notation.
Use a given iterative formula x(n+1) = F(x(n)) to find a root to a given accuracy.
Use standard vector notations: column vectors, xi + yj + zk and AB.
Add and subtract vectors, multiply by a scalar, and interpret these geometrically.
Calculate vector magnitudes and use unit, displacement and position vectors.
Understand the symbols in r = a + tb and find the equation of a line.
Decide whether two lines are parallel, intersecting or skew, and find any intersection point.
Use the scalar product to find angles and perpendicular feet in line and point problems.
Formulate a simple rate-of-change statement as a differential equation.
Find a general solution of a first-order separable differential equation by integration.
Use an initial condition to find a particular solution.
Interpret the solution of a differential equation in the modelled context.
Understand complex numbers, real and imaginary parts, modulus, argument and conjugate, and when two are equal.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide complex numbers in Cartesian form.
Use the fact that non-real roots of real-coefficient polynomials come in conjugate pairs.
Represent complex numbers on an Argand diagram.
Multiply and divide complex numbers in polar form.
Find the two square roots of a complex number.
Understand the geometrical effects of conjugating, adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing complex numbers.
Illustrate simple equations and inequalities with loci on an Argand diagram.
Use the formula for Poisson probabilities Po(lambda).
Use the fact that a Poisson variable has mean and variance both equal to lambda.
Understand how the Poisson distribution models random events, and use it as a model.
Use the Poisson as an approximation to the binomial where appropriate.
Use the normal distribution, with continuity correction, to approximate the Poisson where appropriate.
Use the results for E(aX + b), Var(aX + b), E(aX + bY) and Var(aX + bY) for independent X and Y, and the closure of normal and Poisson distributions under combinations.
Understand a continuous random variable and recall and use properties of a probability density function.
Use a probability density function for probabilities, and to calculate mean and variance.
Understand sample versus population and why random sampling matters.
Explain simply why a given sampling method may be unsatisfactory.
Recognise a sample mean as a random variable with E(X-bar) = mu and Var(X-bar) = sigma^2/n.
Use the fact that the sample mean is normal if X is normal.
Use the Central Limit Theorem where appropriate.
Calculate unbiased estimates of the population mean and variance from raw or summarised data.
Determine and interpret a confidence interval for a population mean with known variance or a large sample.
Determine an approximate confidence interval for a population proportion from a large sample.
Understand hypothesis tests: one- and two-tailed tests, null and alternative hypotheses, significance level, critical region and test statistic.
Carry out a hypothesis test for a single binomial or Poisson observation, directly or with a normal approximation.
Carry out a hypothesis test for a population mean with known variance or a large sample.

subtopics.title: Type I and Type II errors

outcomes.text: Understand Type I and Type II errors.
Calculate probabilities of Type I and Type II errors in specific normal, binomial or Poisson tests.
